quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #19
										  					
  

60 Questions • Passing Score 50

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Stop only if other cars are coming.

questions.correctAnswerText: Bicycles cross here.
questions.explanation: This sign shows where bicycles cross or ride. Drive slowly and carefully in this area because bicycles often cross or travel near traffic here.

questions.question: You do not have to stop for a school bus with red lights flashing if it is on a private road.
questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: You must stop for a school bus with red lights flashing and the stop arm out. This law applies on both public and private roads.

questions.question: How can you prevent hydroplaning?

options.text: Do not drive fast on wet roads.
Keep your tires properly filled with air.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when your car slides on water between the tires and road. Low tire pressure and worn tread increase hydroplaning risk. Speeding on wet roads also increases the risk.

questions.question: On roadways, bicycles are considered:
questions.correctAnswerText: Vehicles.
questions.explanation: Bicycles are vehicles on roadways. Bicyclists and car drivers must follow the same traffic rules.

questions.question: A car is coming toward you on the left and a bicyclist is on your right. You should:

options.text: Let the car pass, then pass the bike.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the car pass, then pass the bike.
questions.explanation: When you face multiple hazards, handle one at a time. Let the oncoming car pass first. Then pass the bicyclist when it is safe.

questions.question: What should you do if there is a deep puddle ahead on the road?

options.text: Drive at the speed limit to get through it.
Avoid the puddle if you can.
Shift to neutral while driving through the water.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid the puddle if you can.
questions.explanation: Avoid slippery areas like puddles, ice, wet leaves, and oil. The safest driving surface is dry and solid.

questions.question: Backing your vehicle is:

options.text: Dangerous only if you have a helper.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always dangerous.
questions.explanation: Backing up is always dangerous because you cannot see clearly behind your vehicle. Be very careful when backing up.

questions.question: Which statement is correct?

options.text: Use your left foot to brake.
Use your right foot for both braking and accelerating.
Always brake hard to ensure you stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your right foot for both braking and accelerating.
questions.explanation: Use your right foot for both braking and accelerating. Apply the brakes gently with gradual pressure so your vehicle stops smoothly.

questions.question: You are driving slowly and traffic is backing up behind you. What should you do?

options.text: Pull off the road on the right side and let traffic pass.
Do not let other cars pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull off the road on the right side and let traffic pass.
questions.explanation: Driving much slower than other traffic is unsafe. On a two-lane road, if traffic is backing up behind you, pull off to the right and let other cars pass. Only drive well below the speed limit when weather or road conditions require it.

questions.question: What is the main idea of defensive driving?

options.text: Other drivers will do the right thing.
Think about what other drivers might do and be ready to react.

questions.correctAnswerText: Think about what other drivers might do and be ready to react.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means expecting other drivers to make mistakes and being ready to respond safely.

questions.question: If you drink alcohol at a social event, how can you drive safely?

options.text: Get a ride home from a friend who has not been drinking.
Take a cold shower before driving.
Wait 30 minutes after drinking before driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get a ride home from a friend who has not been drinking.
questions.explanation: The best way to avoid drunk driving is to arrange a ride with a sober friend. Coffee and cold showers do not lower your blood alcohol level. Your body needs about one hour to process one drink.

questions.question: A flashing red traffic light works the same way as:
questions.correctAnswerText: A stop sign.
questions.explanation: At a flashing red light, you must stop completely. Then yield to all traffic that does not have to stop.

questions.question: Which of these slows down traffic?

options.text: Slowing down to look at a crash.
Using public transportation instead of driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowing down to look at a crash.
questions.explanation: Slowing down to look at accidents (called rubbernecking) causes traffic jams and should be avoided.

questions.question: When turning left, you must yield to:
questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: When turning left, you must yield to oncoming traffic, pedestrians in the intersection, and any other drivers already in the intersection.

questions.question: You must yield to emergency vehicles:

options.text: When you see flashing red or blue lights or hear a siren.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see flashing red or blue lights or hear a siren.
questions.explanation: You must always yield to emergency vehicles that have flashing lights or sirens on.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: You must drive at this exact speed.
The highest legal speed on this road is 55 mph.
You must drive through the intersection at this speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: The highest legal speed on this road is 55 mph.
questions.explanation: This is a speed limit sign showing the maximum speed allowed. In bad weather like rain, snow, or ice, you should drive slower than the posted limit.

questions.question: Roads freeze quickly when they are:
questions.correctAnswerText: In the shade.
questions.explanation: In cold or wet weather, shaded areas under trees or buildings freeze faster than other parts of the road. These areas also take longer to dry.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: A divided highway is starting ahead.
The road ahead will be slippery.

questions.correctAnswerText: A divided highway is starting ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that a divided highway is coming. Stay to the right of the center divider.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.correctAnswerText: Stop Sign Ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a stop sign is coming up ahead.

questions.question: When driving on a slippery surface like snow or ice:

options.text: Shift to low gear before going down steep hills.
Follow other vehicles closely to maintain traction.
Pump your brakes to keep them from freezing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift to low gear before going down steep hills.
questions.explanation: To avoid skidding on slippery surfaces, shift to low gear before going downhill. Keep a larger distance between you and other vehicles. Avoid sudden stops. If you don't have antilock brakes, pump your brakes gently to stop.

questions.question: After passing a vehicle on the left, when is it safe to move back into the right lane?

options.text: When you can no longer see the vehicle over your right shoulder.
When you can see the front of the vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see the front of the vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: You can move back into the right lane when you see the headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror. Always signal before changing lanes.

questions.question: Where should your car be positioned before making a right turn?

options.text: Near the center of the street.
Close to the left side of the street.
Close to the right side of the street.
Past the center of the intersection when you begin to turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Close to the right side of the street.
questions.explanation: Get as far to the right side of the road as possible before making a right turn. Do not cut across other lanes of traffic.

questions.question: A driver does not need to allow as much distance when following a motorcycle as when following a car.
questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: Motorcycles can stop faster than cars in dry conditions. Keep three to four seconds of following distance behind a motorcycle so the rider has time to move in an emergency.

questions.question: Why is it more dangerous to drive at night than during the day?

options.text: You cannot see as far ahead at night.
The road is always more slippery at night.
Your reaction time is slower at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot see as far ahead at night.
questions.explanation: At night, you cannot see as far ahead because of low visibility and glare from oncoming headlights. Always use your headlights and drive carefully in the dark.

questions.question: What should you do if you see an animal on the roadway?

options.text: The driver should honk their horn.
The driver should pass the animal as closely as possible.
The driver should be very cautious.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver should be very cautious.
questions.explanation: Be very cautious when you see an animal on the roadway. Pass it slowly to avoid scaring it.

questions.question: What should you do when bad weather makes it hard to see?

options.text: Speed up to get off the road quickly.
Drive in the lane closest to oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your following distance.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when visibility is poor. This gives you more time to react to hazards you may not see in advance.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Stop only if other cars are approaching.

questions.correctAnswerText: Bicycle crossing.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert drivers that bicycles may be crossing in this area.

questions.question: What does this sign prevent?

options.text: Entrances from the wrong direction on one-way streets and expressway ramps.

questions.correctAnswerText: Entrances from the wrong direction on one-way streets and expressway ramps.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that traffic on this road is one-way. You cannot enter from your current direction.

questions.question: What should you do before entering a curve?
questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce your speed.
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed before a curve. You may drive slower than the posted speed limit for safety, but never faster. Slow down on curves, hills with limited visibility, slippery roads, and roads with animals or pedestrians.

questions.question: What does a single dashed yellow line separating traffic mean?

options.text: Drivers may pass if it is safe to do so.
Both lanes travel in the same direction.
Drivers may pass, even if it could be dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers may pass if it is safe to do so.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. A single dashed yellow line means vehicles in both directions can pass. Only pass if it is safe and you will not interfere with oncoming traffic.

questions.question: Which road surface freezes first?
questions.correctAnswerText: A bridge
questions.explanation: Bridges freeze before the rest of the road. They also thaw out after regular pavement.

questions.question: Distracted driving usually:

options.text: Slows your reaction time to hazards.
Is only dangerous for young drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slows your reaction time to hazards.
questions.explanation: Distractions slow your reaction time. Distracted driving is never safe.

questions.question: When you see orange construction signs and cones on a freeway, you must:

options.text: Slow down because the lane ends ahead.
Be ready for workers and equipment ahead.
Change lanes and keep your current speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready for workers and equipment ahead.
questions.explanation: Work zone signs warn you about workers, slow equipment, and closed lanes. Reduce your speed and be ready to slow down or stop.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Cars in the right lane must slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Merge.
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign means traffic is merging from the right. Be ready to let traffic merge safely.

questions.question: Driving slower than other traffic is:

options.text: A good idea if the weather is bad.
Okay if you don't know the speed limit.
Often dangerous because drivers behind you may try to pass unsafely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Often dangerous because drivers behind you may try to pass unsafely.
questions.explanation: Driving much slower than other traffic frustrates drivers behind you. They may take dangerous risks to pass you.

questions.question: If your tire blows out:

options.text: Slow down gradually and brake lightly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gradually and brake lightly.
questions.explanation: Take your foot off the gas and let the car slow down. Use light braking only after the vehicle slows.

questions.question: At a flashing yellow light, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down, check for cross traffic, and continue with caution.

questions.question: When passing on a multilane highway:

options.text: Make sure the passing lane is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure the passing lane is clear.
questions.explanation: Check that the passing lane is clear before passing. Use your turn signal to show you are changing lanes.

questions.question: Drivers don't have to yield to pedestrians crossing against the traffic light.
questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: You must always yield to pedestrians. Pedestrians may misjudge lights and cross when they shouldn't.

questions.question: Double solid yellow lines mean you may pass from either direction.
questions.correctAnswerText: FALSE
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean no passing in either direction.

questions.question: After a train passes at a railroad crossing, what should you do?

options.text: Wait for the signal lights to stop flashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: After a train passes, watch for a second train on any track. Do not drive until all gates are up and all warning lights stop flashing.

questions.question: What can you do from the center turn lane?
questions.correctAnswerText: You may make left turns.
questions.explanation: This lane is only for left turns from either direction. You cannot use it to pass other cars or drive straight.

questions.question: You are waiting at a stop sign behind other cars. After the cars ahead go through and there is no traffic, what must you do?

options.text: You may go through without stopping again.
You must stop at the stop sign before going.
You may slowly roll past the stop sign.
You may follow the car ahead without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must stop at the stop sign before going.
questions.explanation: You must always make a complete stop at a stop sign. Check for traffic before going. Do not skip this step just because other cars are moving.

questions.question: Why should you use your headlights on rainy, snowy, or foggy days?

options.text: So other drivers can see your car.
To warn others about bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: So other drivers can see your car.
questions.explanation: Bad weather makes it hard to see cars. Your headlights help other drivers spot your vehicle. If you need windshield wipers, turn on your low beam headlights too.

questions.question: At a red light with a green arrow, when can you go in the direction of the arrow?

options.text: After you come to a complete stop.
If you are in the correct lane and the intersection is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: If you are in the correct lane and the intersection is clear.
questions.explanation: A green arrow lets you go if you are in the right lane and the intersection is clear. Always let pedestrians and other cars in the intersection go first.

questions.question: At a four-way stop, you must yield to any driver:
questions.correctAnswerText: Who arrived before you.
questions.explanation: Cars go in the order they arrive. If two cars arrive at the same time, the car on the right goes first.

questions.question: Why are barriers, drums, cones, and signs placed in work zones?

options.text: To make drivers angry about slow traffic.
To keep traffic away from hazards where workers are.

questions.correctAnswerText: To keep traffic away from hazards where workers are.
questions.explanation: Work zones are dangerous for both workers and drivers. Cones, barrels, signs, big trucks, and workers in bright vests warn you about hazards.

questions.question: What should you do when driving through a work zone?

options.text: Speed up to get through quickly.
Slow down and be ready to stop suddenly.
Keep your normal speed through the zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop suddenly.
questions.explanation: Slow down in work zones and be prepared to stop. Follow posted speed limits and watch for workers.

questions.question: When you see this sign, what must you do?

options.text: Stop completely and check for pedestrians and cross traffic.
Stop and wait for a green light.
Slow down and check for traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely and check for pedestrians and cross traffic.
questions.explanation: An eight-sided sign is a stop sign. You must stop completely and look for pedestrians and traffic. Wait for the intersection to clear before going.

questions.question: What is the correct way to make a right turn?

options.text: Signal, slow down, and move to the lane closest to the centerline before turning.
Signal, slow down, and move to the lane closest to the right curb before turning.
Stay near the right curb as you approach, then move toward the middle before turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, slow down, and move to the lane closest to the right curb before turning.
questions.explanation: Signal before turning. Slow down and use the right lane. Stay as close as possible to the right curb or edge of the road.

questions.question: When an emergency vehicle approaches with a siren and/or flashing lights, you must immediately:

options.text: Pull to the right and stop.
Pull to the right and slow down.
Pull to the right and turn on your four-way flashers.
Stop and let the emergency vehicle pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the right and stop.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle with lights and sirens approaches, drive to the right side of the road and stop immediately.

questions.question: You are on the freeway and traffic is merging into your lane. You should:

options.text: Make room for the merging traffic, if possible.
Speed up to keep your position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make room for the merging traffic, if possible.
questions.explanation: When traffic allows, make room for vehicles to merge into your lane.

questions.question: When driving at night, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther behind other vehicles.
questions.explanation: At night, increase the distance between your vehicle and the one ahead because it is harder to see. Use your headlights correctly. Do not look directly at oncoming headlights because the glare can blind you.

questions.question: What do speed limit signs show?

options.text: The highest or lowest speed you are allowed to drive
The speed to drive in heavy traffic
The speed to drive in bad conditions

questions.correctAnswerText: The highest or lowest speed you are allowed to drive
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs show the highest or lowest speed allowed on a road. The maximum speed is for good conditions. You must slow down when conditions are not ideal.

questions.question: At an intersection with no traffic control, you arrive at the same time as vehicles on your left and right. You should:

options.text: Yield to the vehicle on your left.
Yield to the vehicle on your right.
Wait until no vehicles are at the intersection before going.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to the vehicle on your right.
questions.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection where multiple vehicles arrive at the same time, the vehicle on your right has the right-of-way. Then drivers proceed in the order they arrived.

questions.question: You can drive at the maximum posted speed limit only:
questions.correctAnswerText: When conditions are good.
questions.explanation: The posted maximum speed is the fastest legal speed under good conditions. Drive at the same speed as other traffic, but not faster than the limit. All drivers must maintain a safe speed at all times.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.correctAnswerText: Two-way traffic.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that you are leaving a divided highway and entering a road where traffic flows both ways.

questions.question: You are approaching a railroad crossing with a crossbuck sign but no gates or flashing lights. You should:

options.text: Approach slowly and cross only when you are sure no train is coming.
Turn down your radio to listen for a train.
Only cross when a flagger tells you it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Approach all railroad crossings with caution and cross only when you know no train is coming from either direction. Listen for trains and obey any flagger at the crossing.

questions.question: You must obey school crossing guards:
questions.correctAnswerText: At all times.
questions.explanation: Always watch for school crossing guards near schools and obey their instructions at all times.

questions.question: When driving near heavy trucks, you must allow for:

options.text: The longer stopping distance needed by large trucks.
The shorter stopping distance needed by large trucks.
The quieter noise from larger trucks.
The faster speed of larger trucks.

questions.correctAnswerText: The longer stopping distance needed by large trucks.
questions.explanation: Heavy trucks need more distance to stop than smaller vehicles. Stay in a position where the truck driver can see you and where your view of traffic is not blocked by the truck.
